title: Final integration check of Lantern Keep
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#: title screen (New Game, Continue, Settings, Quit), three rooms joined by doors with fades, WASD player (rebindable), a keeper NPC in the hall with a three-line typed dialogue, a pause menu (Resume, Settings, Save, Quit to Title), settings (master volume, fullscreen, vsync, key rebinding), save/continue of room and position, a custom cursor on menus hidden in play, a backtick dev console with `room <name>`, debug logging of room changes and crash reports. All of it has been built by earlier beads. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to do: verify the whole game end to end and fix only small wiring faults found (file new work for anything larger). Do not add features.
- Every module in MODULES.md is installed, wired into the real game (not only a test) and prints its marker: TransitionKit, RunSaveKit, SettingsKit, InputRemapKit, CursorKit, DevConsoleKit, DebugLogKit, CrashKit.
- Check each contract below in the project.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The player node is in the group `player`; the keeper NPC is in the group `keeper`.
- The main scene (`run/main_scene` in `project.godot`) is the title screen. The room scenes are `res://rooms/courtyard.tscn`, `res://rooms/hall.tscn` and `res://rooms/tower.tscn`, and each has the player.
- The dialogue box is a node in the group `dialogue` that becomes visible after interact is pressed near the keeper.
- An input action `interact` exists.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; `godot --headless --path . --quit-after 300` prints all eight module markers, the game's own ready lines and no `ERROR:`; the MoveCheck from MODULES.md passes in each of the three rooms; run/main_scene points at the title screen; a manual play-through of title -> courtyard -> hall (talk to keeper) -> tower -> pause/save -> quit -> Continue works.
Modules: TransitionKit, RunSaveKit, SettingsKit, InputRemapKit, CursorKit, DevConsoleKit, DebugLogKit, CrashKit

title: Developer console on backtick with a room command (DevConsoleKit)
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. Rooms (courtyard, hall, tower) change by name through a room-change service in game code that uses TransitionKit. Mouse mode goes through CursorKit's Push/Pop stack. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build:
- Install DevConsoleKit (`artifactory install DevConsoleKit`), register its DevConsoleManager autoload and instance its DevConsole.tscn under a CanvasLayer as MODULES.md and its README describe, so the console can be opened from the title screen and from every room. Use its UI, history and dispatcher; do not write your own console.
- The console toggles with the backtick key (DevConsoleKit's default toggle action). Make sure console access is enabled when running the game from the project (its access flag is off outside the editor by default; enable it for debug builds through its documented switch).
- Add a game command handler (a BaseCommandHandler subclass) with `room <name>`: `room hall` changes to the hall with the normal fade through the room-change service; an unknown name prints an error listing courtyard, hall, tower.
- While the console is open, the cursor is visible (Push/Pop through CursorKit) and the player does not move.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; a headless run prints `[DevConsoleKit] live` and no `ERROR:`; pressing backtick opens the console; `help` lists `room`; `room tower` fades to the tower with the player present; `room nowhere` prints an error; backtick closes it.
Modules: DevConsoleKit

title: Custom cursor on menus, hidden during play (CursorKit)
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. It has a title screen, a settings screen, a pause menu and a dialogue box over the rooms. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build:
- Install CursorKit (`artifactory install CursorKit`) and register its InputModeManager autoload as MODULES.md says. All mouse-mode changes go through its Push/Pop stack; no script may set Input.MouseMode directly. Do not write your own cursor-mode stack.
- During play in a room the cursor is hidden (push a hidden/captured mode while a room is active). Each menu or overlay (title screen, pause menu, settings screen) pushes a visible mode when it opens and pops it when it closes, so the cursor shows on menus and hides again when play resumes.
- Custom cursor image: CursorKit only owns the mode, so the builder writes this part: add a small custom arrow cursor image (a simple PNG drawn for this game) and set it as the mouse cursor so menus show it instead of the system arrow.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; a headless run prints `[CursorKit] live` and no `ERROR:`; the title screen shows the custom cursor; starting a game hides it; opening the pause menu or settings shows it again; resuming hides it; quitting to title shows it.
Modules: CursorKit

title: Dialogue box that types out the keeper's three lines
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. The keeper NPC in the hall (group `keeper`) fires a conversation trigger when the player presses interact in range. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build (no module covers dialogue; the builder writes it):
- A dialogue box UI (a panel at the bottom of the screen) that is hidden until the keeper's conversation starts. The node joins group `dialogue` in code.
- The keeper has three lines of text (write three short in-world lines about the keep and its lantern). On start, the box becomes visible and the first line types out letter by letter. Each further press of interact: if the line is still typing, finish it at once; otherwise show the next line. After the third line, the next press closes the box.
- While the box is open the player does not move, and interact does not restart the conversation.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The dialogue box is a node in the group `dialogue` that becomes visible after interact is pressed near the keeper.
- The player node is in the group `player`; the keeper NPC is in the group `keeper`.
- An input action `interact` exists.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds with no `ERROR:` in a headless run; in the hall, walking to the keeper and pressing interact makes the node in group `dialogue` visible with line 1 typing out; presses advance through all three lines, one per press, and then close it; the player can walk again afterwards.
Modules: none

title: Save and Continue: persist current room and player position (RunSaveKit)
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. There are three rooms (courtyard, hall, tower) and a room-change service that can load a room by name, optionally with a spawn position. The pause menu has a Save button hook and the title screen has a disabled Continue button with a hook. The player is the node in group `player`. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build:
- Install RunSaveKit (`artifactory install RunSaveKit`). Use its SaveSlot for writing and reading the save file (atomic write, versioning, recovery); do not write your own file saving.
- Pause menu Save writes the current room name and the player's position to the save slot and shows a brief "Saved" confirmation.
- Title screen Continue is enabled only when a valid save loads; pressing it fades into the saved room (through the room-change service) and places the player at the saved position.
- A missing or corrupt save leaves Continue disabled and never crashes.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The player node is in the group `player`; the keeper NPC is in the group `keeper`.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; a headless run prints `[RunSaveKit] live` and no `ERROR:`; walk to the tower, move somewhere, Save, quit the game, relaunch: Continue is enabled and puts the player in the tower at the saved spot. With the save file deleted, Continue is disabled.
Modules: RunSaveKit

title: Pause menu on Escape: Resume, Settings, Save, Quit to Title

What to build (no module covers a pause menu; the builder writes it):
- Pressing the pause action (Escape) while in a room pauses the game (the player stops moving) and shows a pause menu with Resume, Settings, Save, Quit to Title. Escape again or Resume closes it and unpauses.
- Settings opens the existing settings screen over the pause menu; Back returns to the pause menu.
- Save: leave a hook for the save bead to fill in (the button can show a short "Saved" note once that bead is done).
- Quit to Title unpauses and fades back to the title screen through TransitionKit (not a fade of your own).

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds with no `ERROR:` in a headless run; in a room, Escape freezes the player and shows the menu; Resume and Escape both resume; Settings opens and returns; Quit to Title fades to the title screen.
Modules: TransitionKit

title: Key rebinding in the settings screen (InputRemapKit)
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. The player moves with input actions move_forward, move_back, move_left, move_right (WASD) and uses interact (E). A settings screen exists (built with SettingsKit) with a space reserved for key rebinding. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build:
- Install InputRemapKit (`artifactory install InputRemapKit`) and register its InputRemapManager autoload as MODULES.md says. Use it for remapping, conflict checks and saving bindings; do not write your own binding storage or conflict detection.
- In the settings screen, add a row per rebindable action (the four move actions and interact) showing its display name and current key, with a button that waits for the next key press and rebinds the action to it. If the key is already used by another action, show which one and do not apply it. Add a "Reset keys" button that restores defaults.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- An input action `interact` exists.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; a headless run prints `[InputRemapKit] live` and no `ERROR:`; rebinding move_forward to another key makes the player walk forward with that key in a room, the binding survives a restart, a conflicting key is refused with a message, and Reset keys restores WASD/E. MoveCheck still passes with default bindings.
Modules: InputRemapKit

title: Doors between rooms with fade transition (TransitionKit)
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#. Three rooms exist at res://rooms/courtyard.tscn, res://rooms/hall.tscn and res://rooms/tower.tscn, each with a player (group `player`) that walks with WASD. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md first.

What to build:
- Install TransitionKit (`artifactory install TransitionKit`) and register its autoload as MODULES.md says. Use TransitionManager for every room change; do not write your own fade overlay or scene loader.
- Doors: the courtyard has a door to the hall; the hall has a door back to the courtyard and a door to the tower; the tower has a door back to the hall. A door is a visible marker (for example a coloured doorway block) the player walks into. Walking into it fades to black, loads the target room, and fades back in.
- The player arrives next to the matching door in the new room (not inside it, so they do not bounce straight back). Keep this in a small room-change service of your own (for example an autoload RoomManager with a ChangeRoom(roomName, optional spawn position) call and a CurrentRoom name) so later beads (save/continue, dev console `room` command, debug logging) can change rooms by name ("courtyard", "hall", "tower") through the same path. The door triggers and the room-change service are game code the builder writes; only the fade and scene load come from TransitionKit.

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The room scenes are `res://rooms/courtyard.tscn`, `res://rooms/hall.tscn` and `res://rooms/tower.tscn`, and each has the player.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; a headless run prints `[TransitionKit] live` and no `ERROR:`; walking through each door in play changes to the right room with a fade and the player appears beside the return door; calling the room-change service with each room name loads that room. MoveCheck still passes in each room.
Modules: TransitionKit

title: Set up Lantern Keep project skeleton: input actions, title and room scenes
description:
Game context: Lantern Keep is a small top-down 3D game in Godot 4.7 with C#, in this project. A camera looks down on capsule-style characters. It has a title screen, three rooms (courtyard, hall, tower) joined by doors, a player moving with WASD, a keeper NPC with dialogue, a pause menu, settings, save/continue, a dev console, debug logging and crash reports. Later beads build those; this bead lays the ground they stand on. Read AGENTS.md and MODULES.md in the project root before starting; follow their project-file formats and pitfalls exactly.

What to build (no module covers this; the builder writes it):
- project.godot: application name "Lantern Keep"; the main scene is a title screen scene (for example res://ui/title.tscn). For now the title scene can be an empty Control with a "Lantern Keep" label; a later bead adds its buttons.
- Input actions under [input], bound by physical key: move_forward (W), move_back (S), move_left (A), move_right (D), interact (E), pause (Escape).
- Three room scenes at exactly res://rooms/courtyard.tscn, res://rooms/hall.tscn and res://rooms/tower.tscn. For now each is a Node3D root with a script that prints a ready line (for example "[Room] courtyard ready"). A later bead adds geometry and the player.
- Copy MoveCheck.cs from MODULES.md into the project root and register it as an autoload, as MODULES.md describes (it will only pass once the player bead is done).

Contracts (copy of the game brief; must hold):
- The main scene (`run/main_scene` in `project.godot`) is the title screen. The room scenes are `res://rooms/courtyard.tscn`, `res://rooms/hall.tscn` and `res://rooms/tower.tscn`, and each has the player.
- An input action `interact` exists.
- The project builds with `dotnet build`.
(The "each has the player" part is finished by the player and rooms beads; here just create the three scenes at those paths.)

Done when: `dotnet build` succeeds; `godot --headless --path . --quit-after 300` prints no `ERROR:` line and shows the title scene's ready line; project.godot lists all six input actions and run/main_scene points at the title scene.
